title: Why the diagonal Jacobi sum lives in ℤ[ζ_n]
content: For a multiplicative character $\chi$ of order dividing $n$ on a finite field $F$, the **Jacobi sum** $J(\chi,\chi) = \sum_{x} \chi(x)\,\chi(1-x)$ is an algebraic integer that lies in the cyclotomic subring $\mathbb{Z}[\zeta_n] = \texttt{Algebra.adjoin } \mathbb{Z}\,\{\mu\}$ generated by a primitive $n$-th root of unity $\mu$, not merely in the ambient codomain $R$. Each character value is a power of $\mu$, so every term $\chi(x)\chi(1-x)$ is a product of elements of $\mathbb{Z}[\mu]$, and the sum stays inside the subring. This integrality is the structural prerequisite of the higher power-reciprocity laws: the cubic and quartic reciprocity symbols are read off $J(\chi,\chi)$ modulo a prime of $\mathbb{Z}[\zeta_n]$, which only makes sense once $J(\chi,\chi)$ is known to live there.

title: jacobiSum_self_mem_algebraAdjoin — the diagonal case
content: The diagonal specialization $J(\chi,\chi) \in \mathbb{Z}[\mu]$, obtained from Mathlib's general two-character lemma `jacobiSum_mem_algebraAdjoin_of_pow_eq_one` by setting $\varphi := \chi$ and supplying the single hypothesis $\chi^n = 1$ in both argument slots. One line: `jacobiSum_mem_algebraAdjoin_of_pow_eq_one hχ hχ hμ`. This is the exact form the higher-reciprocity application invokes, since the reciprocity symbol is read off the diagonal sum $J(\chi,\chi)$.

title: jacobiSum_self_mem_algebraAdjoin_of_orderOf — the order bridge
content: The same conclusion phrased from $\texttt{orderOf } \chi = n$, the hypothesis available downstream where a character arrives with its order (3 for cubic, 4 for quartic reciprocity). `pow_orderOf_eq_one χ` gives $\chi^{\,\texttt{orderOf }\chi} = 1$; rewriting through the order equality with `▸` yields $\chi^n = 1$, then the first theorem applies. The rewrite is valid because `MulChar F R` is a `CommGroup`, hence a `Monoid`, so `pow_orderOf_eq_one` is available.
prerequisites: group theory: order of an element

title: jacobiSum_isIntegral — upgrading membership to algebraic integrality
content: Mathlib's lemma only places $J(\chi,\varphi)$ in the *subring* $\mathbb{Z}[\mu]$; this theorem upgrades that to genuine `IsIntegral ℤ`, the honest meaning of "Jacobi sums are algebraic integers." The chain is three steps: (1) $\mu$ is a primitive root of unity, hence integral over $\mathbb{Z}$ (`IsPrimitiveRoot.isIntegral`, needing $0 < n$ from `NeZero`); (2) therefore the singly-generated subalgebra $\mathbb{Z}[\mu]$ is *module-finite* over $\mathbb{Z}$ (`IsIntegral.fg_adjoin_singleton`); (3) every element of a finite $\mathbb{Z}$-subalgebra is integral over $\mathbb{Z}$ (`IsIntegral.of_mem_of_fg`). Membership $J(\chi,\varphi) \in \mathbb{Z}[\mu]$ feeds step (3) as the witness.

title: jacobiSum_self_isIntegral (+ of_orderOf) — the diagonal cyclotomic integer
content: The diagonal specializations $\varphi := \chi$ of the integrality upgrade: `jacobiSum_self_isIntegral` proves $J(\chi,\chi)$ is integral over $\mathbb{Z}$ from $\chi^n = 1$, and `jacobiSum_self_isIntegral_of_orderOf` rebases that on $\texttt{orderOf }\chi = n$ through the same `pow_orderOf_eq_one` bridge. This is the precise sense in which $J(\chi,\chi)$ is a cyclotomic *integer*: a member of $\mathbb{Z}[\zeta_n]$ that is genuinely integral over $\mathbb{Z}$, hence whose reduction modulo a prime ideal of $\mathbb{Z}[\zeta_n]$ is well-defined — exactly what the cubic and quartic reciprocity symbols require.
